post.description:
Govern a discovered shadow system by creating a real agent and issuing a
capability token (architecture.md sections 5 and 6).

Maps the inferred (or overridden) ``registration_config`` onto the real
``agents`` columns only (``name`` -> ``subject``/``display_name``,
``framework`` -> ``framework``, ``platform``/``model_identifier`` folded into
``metadata``, observed behavior -> ``declared_capabilities``); never inserts a
nonexistent ``name``/``platform``/``model_identifier`` column. Then issues a
capability token from the mapped ``token_recommendation``, flips the
discovered row to ``governed`` and links ``registered_agent_id``. Strictly
org-scoped via explicit ``WHERE org_id = $1``; a system that is already
governed returns 400 and an unknown/cross-org id returns 404.

post.description:
Enable continuous discovery for the caller's org (architecture.md section
8).

Upserts the org's single ``discovery_state`` row (``org_id`` is UNIQUE),
flipping ``continuous_enabled`` to true and persisting the requested
``poll_interval_seconds`` (default 900). ``discovery_state`` is RLS-enforced,
so the write runs after ``set_org_guc(conn, org_id)`` inside a transaction;
the explicit ``WHERE`` on the UNIQUE ``org_id`` keeps it correct on superuser
connections that bypass RLS.

Disable continuous discovery for the caller's org (architecture.md section
8).

Flips ``continuous_enabled`` to false on the org's ``discovery_state`` row
while preserving the persisted ``poll_interval_seconds``. When no row exists
yet one is created (disabled, default interval). RLS-scoped via
``set_org_guc`` inside a transaction.

get.description:
Return the caller org's continuous-discovery state (architecture.md

that never enabled continuous discovery gets the sane default
(``continuous_enabled=false``, ``poll_interval_seconds=900``) rather than a
500. The explicit ``WHERE org_id = $1`` isolates the row on superuser
connections that bypass RLS.

post.description: Suspend an agent.

Reactivate a suspended or revoked agent.

Mission 19: reactivating a revoked agent (e.g. after an org-wide
emergency stop, VAL-KILL-025) restores it to ``active`` and bumps
the revocation epoch so the signed feed advances monotonically
(VAL-KILL-011). Previously only suspended agents could be
reactivated; revoked agents are now also accepted (additive —
existing suspended->active callers are unaffected).

Permanently revoke an agent with cryptographic proof.

This is the MOSS Kill Switch. When an agent is revoked:
1. Agent status is set to 'revoked' - cannot sign any more actions
2. A signed revocation event is created with ML-DSA-44
3. The revocation proof is stored in the audit log
4. The proof can be verified offline to confirm when and why revocation occurred

The revocation record contains:
- Agent ID
- Organization ID
- Revocation timestamp (microsecond precision)
- Reason (if provided)
- Revoking user/API key
- ML-DSA-44 signature over all fields

tagged with ``owner_type`` and an ``inherited`` marker (VAL-POLICY-005/006/007)

post.description:
Create a new policy with version control.

A ``cust_`` (customer) caller creates an owner_type='customer' policy in the
inheritance-aware ``workflow_authorization_policies`` table (scoped to its own
org) and invalidates the org's effective-policy cache so it takes effect on
the next evaluate/sign (VAL-POLICY-016). Any other org credential keeps the
legacy versioned ``policies`` behavior (initial v1 version, immutable, audit).

Dry-run policy evaluation over the org's EFFECTIVE (inherited) policy set.

Resolves system + matching-partner-default + the org's own customer policies
and feeds that ordered set into the EXISTING
``PolicyEngineService.evaluate()`` (no second engine, no execution envelope,
no signature, no persisted violation/escalation). Returns the decision
(``allow`` | ``block`` | ``escalate``) plus the contributing policies, each
tagged with ``owner_type`` so the caller can see which inherited or own
policy drove the outcome. Another partner's default never contributes
(VAL-POLICY-008).

post.description:
Approve a held action with cryptographic proof.

When an action is approved:
1. A signed approval event is created with ML-DSA-44
2. The approval proof includes: who approved, when, the action details
3. The signed proof is stored and can be verified offline
4. The original action is released to proceed

This creates non-repudiable evidence that a human reviewed and approved the action.

Deny a held action with cryptographic proof.

When an action is denied:
1. A signed denial event is created with ML-DSA-44
2. The denial proof includes: who denied, when, the action details, reason
3. The signed proof is stored and can be verified offline
4. The original action is blocked permanently

This creates non-repudiable evidence that a human reviewed and denied the action.

get.description:
Walk the audit chain and report whether it is internally consistent.

Delegates to :func:`signing_api.audit.chain.verify_audit_chain`,
which for every row in chronological order:
  * confirms the row's stored ``previous_hash`` equals the prior
    row's ``entry_hash`` (or the genesis value for the first row)
  * confirms ``entry_hash`` is a valid 64-char hex string
  * **recomputes** ``entry_hash = SHA256(previous_hash ||
    canonical_json(entry))`` from the row's stored content and
    compares it to the stored ``entry_hash`` — this is the check
    that detects a direct DB mutation of payload columns
    (action/subject/parameters/...) that leaves the stored hash
    untouched (BUG-079 / VAL-INTEG-004).

Returns ``{"verified": true, ...}`` when all checks hold for every
row, ``{"verified": false, "broken_at": <row_id>, "broken_index":
<int>, "reason": "..."}`` when the chain has been tampered with via
a direct DB mutation.

post.description:
Test the caller org's PagerDuty integration by dispatching a real event.

Looks up the org's stored PagerDuty Events API v2 routing/integration key
and dispatches a real ``trigger`` test event to PagerDuty. Returns an
honest success/failure based on PagerDuty's response (``202 Accepted`` ->
success; non-2xx/missing key/network error -> failure with a reason).

The test uses the caller org's OWN routing key (org isolation) and never
echoes the routing key or any other secret in the response. Success is
never the unconditional stub value -- it is contingent on PagerDuty's
actual acceptance of the event.

Canonical Stripe webhook endpoint.

Idempotency + retry safety: the ``billing_events`` dedup-marker insert and
the handler's critical DB side effects run inside a SINGLE transaction. If a
handler/DB side effect fails, the transaction (including the dedup marker)
rolls back and the endpoint returns a non-2xx so Stripe retries -- a genuine
failure never leaves a committed ``processed`` marker with no side effects.
A true replay (the marker already exists) short-circuits to
``already_processed`` with no re-processing. Best-effort audit/SIEM + email
run only AFTER the transaction commits, so those failures never trigger a
retry.

POST /v1/scheduled/lifecycle/auto-deactivate-sweep

Sweep every ``suspended`` customer whose 90-day ``auto_deactivate_at``
window has elapsed and transition it to ``deactivated``
(VAL-LIFECYCLE-022). Called by Cloud Scheduler on a schedule (e.g. daily).
Each candidate is transitioned atomically in its own transaction under
``SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`` (re-checking ``status='suspended'`` and
``auto_deactivate_at <= NOW()`` under the lock), so a concurrent sweep or a
concurrent partner reactivate/deactivate cannot race into a
double-transition. The transition row records ``trigger='auto_deactivate'``,
``triggered_by='system:auto'``; the org row is retained (soft deactivate).

Cross-seam fan-out (VAL-CROSS-015): for each deactivated customer the
sweep emits one fire-and-forget ``customer.status_changed`` partner-webhook
event whose payload ``data.previous == 'suspended'`` and
``data.current == 'deactivated'`` with ``trigger='auto_deactivate'`` and
``transitioned_by='system:auto'`` (the system/auto actor), so the SAME
edge is observable on the webhook stream, the delivery log, and the
analytics ``by_status`` / ``trend.churned`` shift simultaneously. Emission
is non-fatal (VAL-WEBHOOK-025): a delivery failure never breaks the sweep.

Auth: gated by :func:`verify_scheduler_auth` (the Cloud Scheduler shared
key); permissive in dev mode when no scheduler key is configured, so the
local test API and the lifecycle test seam can drive the sweep via curl.

POST /v1/scheduled/webhooks/process-retries

Sweep every partner webhook delivery whose ``status='retrying'`` and
``next_retry_at <= NOW()`` and re-POST it on the exponential retry
schedule (VAL-WEBHOOK-020/021/022/033). This is the DETERMINISTIC
validation path for VAL-WEBHOOK-020: the user-testing flow validator
drives retries via this seam (``curl -X POST ... -H 'Authorization:
Bearer <scheduler-key>'``) rather than waiting on wall-clock
``next_retry_at`` deltas. The lifespan background sweeper
(:func:`signing_api.main._webhook_retry_sweeper_loop`) is OFF under
``TESTING=true`` precisely so this seam stays the single deterministic
driver during the pytest gate and the live validation API.

Returns ``{"processed": [<delivery_id>, ...], "count": N}`` where
``processed`` lists the delivery-row PKs handed to the retry worker this
sweep and ``count`` is the number of retry attempts processed. A sweep
with no due deliveries returns ``{"processed": [], "count": 0}``.

Auth: gated by :func:`verify_scheduler_auth` (the Cloud Scheduler shared
key); permissive in dev mode when no scheduler key is configured, mirroring
the ``/scheduled/lifecycle/auto-deactivate-sweep`` pattern. Without a valid
scheduler key (when one is configured) the request is rejected with 403.

Stripe-style at-least-once + exponential backoff (Prakash 2026 capability
paths; Stripe webhook at-least-once + idempotency). The retry schedule,
fresh per-attempt timestamp+signature, incrementing ``X-Moss-Retry-Count``,
and 6-attempt dead-letter + failure alert live in
:meth:`PartnerWebhookService.process_due_retries` / :meth:`_retry_one`; this
endpoint only ensures that path is actually invokable on the live API.

POST /v1/scheduled/webhooks/inject-test-event

Dispatch a partner-webhook event at a caller-specified severity through
the real :meth:`PartnerWebhookService.dispatch_event` path
(VAL-WEBHOOK-018 positive half). Mirrors the established scheduled-task
test-seam convention (``verify_scheduler_auth`` + dev-permissive +
``{processed,count}``-style response) used by
``POST /v1/scheduled/lifecycle/auto-deactivate-sweep`` and
``POST /v1/scheduled/webhooks/process-retries``.

The seam does NOT bypass delivery: it calls the SAME
``PartnerWebhookService.dispatch_event`` the lifecycle emit hook calls,
so verified-before-live gating, subscription matching, the
``severity_minimum`` / ``environments`` filters, the signed ML-DSA-44
envelope, the ``webhook_deliveries`` idempotency row, and the retry
schedule all run as for a production emission. It exists ONLY because the
M2 lifecycle emits a single partner-webhook event
(``customer.status_changed``) hardcoded to ``severity='info'``
(``routes/partner.py``), so there is no black-box path to emit a
high-severity partner-webhook event to exercise the
``severity_minimum`` filter's positive half. Later milestones
(``rl-usage-alerts`` in ``realtime-and-limits``) route REAL high-severity
events (``customer.usage_threshold`` at 100%) to
``partner_webhook_service``; this seam remains for deterministic
validation.

Returns ``{"dispatched": [<outcome>, ...], "count": N}`` where
``dispatched`` lists the outcome dict for each ACTIVE subscribed webhook
that received the event this call (each outcome carries ``webhook_id``,
``event_id``, ``delivery_id``, ``event_type``, ``delivered``, ``status``,
``response_code``, ``error`` — exactly what
:meth:`PartnerWebhookService.dispatch_event` returns). A call that
matches no active webhook (e.g. all filtered out by
``severity_minimum``) returns ``{"dispatched": [], "count": 0}``.

Auth: gated by :func:`verify_scheduler_auth` (the Cloud Scheduler shared
key); permissive in dev mode when no scheduler key is configured, mirroring
the other scheduled webhook seams. Without a valid scheduler key (when one
is configured) the request is rejected with 403.

Stripe-style at-least-once + idempotency (Prakash 2026 capability paths;
Stripe webhook at-least-once + idempotency).

POST /v1/scheduled/analytics-stream/inject-test-event

Publish a ``signature`` / ``violation`` / ``compliance_change`` frame
through the REAL :class:`AnalyticsStreamManager` fan-out path
(VAL-STREAM-005..007 / 009 / 010). Mirrors the established scheduled-task
test-seam convention (``verify_scheduler_auth`` + dev-permissive +
``{dispatched,count}``-style response) used by
``POST /v1/scheduled/webhooks/inject-test-event`` and
``POST /v1/scheduled/webhooks/process-retries``.

The seam does NOT bypass fan-out: it calls the SAME ``publish_*`` methods
the in-process event publishers will call, so the manager's per-partner
registry, send-failure dead-connection handling, and strict partner
scoping all run as for a production emission. It exists ONLY because the
M2 signing / policy / compliance hot paths do not yet wire into the
analytics stream on this milestone; later milestones route REAL events
to the manager, and this seam remains for deterministic validation.

Tenant isolation: ``partner_id`` is resolved from
``organizations.partner_id`` for the supplied ``customer_id`` (with an
explicit ``WHERE id = $1`` predicate), NEVER taken from the request
body. A customer that does not exist or has no partner association
yields ``{"dispatched": False, "count": 0, "error": "customer_not_found"}``
and publishes nothing -- a foreign customer is a nonexistent one
(VAL-STREAM-009/010).

Returns ``{"dispatched": True, "count": N, "partner_id": <pid>}`` where
``count`` is the number of live connections that received the frame
(0 if no partner-owned subscription is currently live; the frame is
still "published" but has no recipient). An unknown ``event_type`` ->
``{"dispatched": False, "count": 0, "error": "unknown_event_type"}``.

Auth: gated by :func:`verify_scheduler_auth` (the Cloud Scheduler shared
key); permissive in dev mode when no scheduler key is configured,
mirroring the other scheduled seams.

Push-over-poll (Parakhin 2026, Capability Coherence); event-sourced
fan-out (Kleppmann DDIA 2017); AAAI 2026 realtime aggregation.

POST /v1/scheduled/analytics-stream/send-heartbeat

Trigger one ``heartbeat`` fan-out tick through the REAL
:meth:`AnalyticsStreamManager.send_heartbeat` path (VAL-STREAM-008).
Mirrors the established scheduled-task test-seam convention
(``verify_scheduler_auth`` + dev-permissive + ``{sent,count}``-style
response) used by ``POST /v1/scheduled/webhooks/process-retries`` and the
inject-test-event seam above.

The seam exists because the production heartbeat loop
(:meth:`AnalyticsStreamManager._heartbeat_loop`) is OFF under
``TESTING=true`` (per the mission convention that background loops stay
deterministic and off during the pytest gate + live validation API), so a
validator driving the live API with ``TESTING=true`` cannot observe a
wall-clock heartbeat without waiting ``PING_INTERVAL_SECONDS``. This seam
drives one heartbeat tick on demand so a validator observes recurring
``heartbeat`` frames (call twice to prove periodicity, VAL-STREAM-008),
confirms ``connected_customers`` reflects the live count after a
disconnect (VAL-STREAM-012/016), and confirms a held connection stays
open across heartbeat ticks (VAL-STREAM-013). The production loop calls
the SAME :meth:`send_heartbeat` on each tick; the seam only owns the
invocation cadence.

Returns ``{"sent": N, "count": N}`` where ``N`` is the number of live
connections that received a heartbeat this tick (0 if no partner holds a
live subscription).

Auth: gated by :func:`verify_scheduler_auth` (the Cloud Scheduler shared
key); permissive in dev mode when no scheduler key is configured,
mirroring the other scheduled seams.

post.description:
Mint a full-access, 15-minute TTL ``cust_`` session token for a customer
the partner owns (VAL-BE-001..014).

The minted token is a real ``cust_`` credential stored hash-only in
``api_keys`` (it authenticates on every customer-scoped route exactly like
a customer's own token) with two additions: a 15-minute ``expires_at``
(enforced by the shared resolver, VAL-BE-004/005) and a ``name`` marker
``partner-session:{prt_prefix}`` attributing it to the issuing partner
(VAL-BE-014). The raw token is returned exactly once; only its sha256 is
persisted (VAL-BE-013).

Auth + rate limiting are inherited via ``Depends(get_partner)`` (401 on
missing/invalid ``prt_``, 403 ``invalid_credential_type`` on a wrong-prefix
credential, 429 + ``Retry-After`` on a burst beyond the partner budget,
VAL-BE-007/008/009/011). An unknown / cross-partner ``customer_id`` returns
404 ``customer_not_found`` (existence-non-leak, never 403, VAL-BE-006). A
``deactivated`` (terminal) customer is rejected with 409
``customer_not_active`` (defined outcome, no silent status flip); any other
status is accepted and the mint NEVER touches ``organizations.status``
(VAL-BE-012 — a ``pending`` customer stays ``pending`` after the mint).

(same ``session_id`` + same raw ``cust_`` token, no second ``api_keys``
row); a same-key/different-customer replay is a 409
``idempotency_key_conflict``. An audit event ``partner.session.minted`` is

post.description:
Register a new PENDING account and send an email-verification link.

Creates the user (``email_verified=false``), a pending organization with no
plan and no product entitlements, and an owner membership; no session is
created, so the response carries only a verification prompt. The
verification email is best-effort: a Resend failure is logged and does not
roll back the account. Duplicate emails return 400 with a generic message.

Consume an email-verification token, then authenticate the user.

A valid, unused, unexpired token marks the user ``email_verified`` and mints
a session + ``__Secure-moss-session`` cookie, returning a redirect to the
(still pending) dashboard. The token is single-use and the claim is
concurrency-safe. A token whose owner is already verified is idempotent: it
returns the same redirect but mints no second session. Invalid/used/expired
tokens are rejected with 400 and set no cookie. The account stays pending --
verification gates login, not product access.

Re-issue a verification email for an unverified account, without leaking.

For an unverified account under the hourly limit, a fresh 24h token is
created and emailed. Unknown emails and already-verified emails return the
same generic 200 with no token and no email (no enumeration). An unverified
account that has already been issued the per-hour maximum is throttled with
429. The email send is best-effort: a Resend failure is logged and does not
surface an error.

Issue a password-reset email for the given address.

Always returns 200 with the same message whether or not an account exists,
so the response can never be used to enumerate registered emails. The reset
token is generated and stored only for a real user; the email send is
best-effort and a Resend failure is logged without surfacing an error.

Complete a password reset with a token issued by ``/password-reset``.

A valid, unused, unexpired token updates the user's password, is consumed
single-use, invalidates the user's other outstanding reset tokens, and
deletes all of the user's sessions so every device must re-authenticate. The
new-password strength is enforced by the request schema, so a weak password
is rejected (422) before the token is touched and the token stays reusable.
Invalid/used/expired tokens are rejected with 400. Email-verification tokens
are never accepted here -- they live in a separate table.

viewer/insufficient-role caller gets 403 with no agents stopped
and the epoch unchanged (VAL-KILL-024). A cross-org caller is

policy DENY, or ``status=="uncertain"`` (fail-and-report) on a policy ESCALATE
or an over-ceiling / aggregation risk. All three are HTTP 200; only an invalid
capability or a malformed request is a 4xx.

The sign is bounded by a hard latency ceiling (architecture.md §7: 100ms
hard limit; ``MOSS_SIGN_HARD_LIMIT_MS`` env, further tightenable per request
via ``X-MOSS-Max-Sign-Latency-Ms``). A sign that cannot complete within the
ceiling is shed with 503 + ``Retry-After`` rather than returning a
late-signed 200 (VAL-SIGN-026); the in-flight signing transaction is
cancelled, so no envelope is persisted.

IntrospectRequest.title: IntrospectRequest
IntrospectRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /v1/tokens/introspect`` (RFC 7662 §2.1).

``token`` is required: a missing field is a 422 ``validation_error``
(VAL-BE-043), NOT 200 ``{active: false}``. The value may be any string;
prefix dispatch happens in the service layer (an unrecognized prefix is
``{active: false}``, not a 422 — VAL-BE-026).

IntrospectResponse.title: IntrospectResponse
IntrospectResponse.description:
OpenAPI response schema for ``POST /v1/tokens/introspect`` (200).

RFC 7662-style: ``active`` is always present (boolean); ``token_type`` is
one of ``partner`` / ``customer`` / ``capability`` for active tokens and
absent for inactive ones (VAL-BE-023 returns exactly ``{active: false}``
with no identity fields). Identity / scope / expiry fields
(``partner_id`` / ``customer_id`` / ``org_id`` / ``token_id`` /
``subject_agent_id`` / ``exp`` / ``scope`` / ...) are carried selectively
by active tokens; they are declared optional here so the OpenAPI schema
advertises them without forcing them onto the inactive response.

This model is referenced ONLY via the route's ``responses`` parameter for
OpenAPI documentation — it is NOT a ``response_model`` — so the runtime
response body is serialized unchanged (no field filtering), preserving
VAL-BE-020..023 + VAL-BE-026 wire behavior exactly (VAL-DX-015b).

MintSessionResponse.title: MintSessionResponse
MintSessionResponse.description:
Response body for ``POST /v1/partner/customers/{id}/session`` (201).

Exactly the five fields returned by the mint (VAL-BE-001, VAL-DX-015a):
``session_id`` (the ``api_keys.id`` of the session row), ``customer_id``
(echoes the path id), ``token`` (the raw ``cust_`` credential, returned
exactly once), ``prefix`` (the ``cust_`` prefix), and ``expires_at``
(ISO-8601, ~15 minutes out). Used as the route's ``response_model`` so
FastAPI emits a precise OpenAPI 201 schema with all five fields required.
The route already returns exactly these fields, so ``response_model``
filtering is a no-op on the wire.

ReactivateCustomerRequest.title: ReactivateCustomerRequest
ReactivateCustomerRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /v1/partner/customers/{id}/reactivate`` (M2 extension).

``resolution`` is REQUIRED at the domain layer (VAL-LIFECYCLE-020): a
reactivate with no body or an incomplete resolution (``issue_resolved``
false / ``details`` empty) is rejected with 422 ``missing_resolution`` and
no state change. The field is declared Optional here so the domain
:class:`MissingResolutionError` (raised from the service layer) produces
the canonical ``missing_resolution`` error code rather than a FastAPI
Pydantic ``validation_error`` (aligns with the AGENTS.md lifecycle
exception->HTTP map). Reactivation restores EXACTLY the pre-suspension
state (sandbox stays sandbox, production stays production), reactivates the
customer's agents, and closes the active suspension bookkeeping while
retaining the historical suspension record for audit.

ReactivateResolutionRequest.title: ReactivateResolutionRequest
ReactivateResolutionRequest.description:
Resolution record required for ``suspended -> <prior>`` (VAL-LIFECYCLE-020).

``issue_resolved`` MUST be ``true`` and ``details`` MUST be a non-empty
remediation note, or the reactivate is rejected with 422
``missing_resolution`` and no side effect (no status flip, no transition
row, no agent reactivation). The sub-fields are declared Optional/defaults
here so the domain :class:`MissingResolutionError` (raised from the service
layer) produces the canonical ``missing_resolution`` error code rather than
a FastAPI Pydantic ``validation_error`` (aligns with the AGENTS.md
lifecycle exception->HTTP map). The resolution is recorded into the
immutable ``customer_state_transitions`` row's metadata and into the
retained ``suspension_history`` entry so the reactivation is auditable (the
lifecycle log is event-sourced, Kleppmann DDIA 2017).

_AnalyticsStreamInjectRequest.title: _AnalyticsStreamInjectRequest
_AnalyticsStreamInjectRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /v1/scheduled/analytics-stream/inject-test-event``.

The seam publishes a ``signature`` / ``violation`` / ``compliance_change``
frame through the REAL :class:`AnalyticsStreamManager` fan-out path (it
is NOT a socket bypass): the manager resolves the partner's live
connections from its in-process registry and pushes the frame to each.
The seam exists because the M2 in-process event publishers for
signatures / violations / compliance changes are not yet wired through
the signing / policy / compliance hot paths on this milestone (the
analytics stream is net-new in ``realtime-and-limits``); without a
deterministic black-box path, VAL-STREAM-005..007 / 009 / 010 cannot be
exercised end-to-end against the live API. Later milestones route REAL
signing / policy / compliance events to the manager; the seam remains
for deterministic validation.

``partner_id`` is NOT client-supplied: the seam resolves it from
``organizations.partner_id`` for the supplied ``customer_id`` (with an
explicit ``WHERE id = $1`` predicate), so a caller cannot push a frame
to another partner's stream -- tenant isolation is preserved
(VAL-STREAM-009/010).

partner_id.title: Partner Id
partner_id.description: Owning partner id (the event is scoped to this partner)

customer_id.title: Customer Id
customer_id.description: Optional customer (org) id the event pertains to

event_id.title: Event Id
event_id.description: Optional stable logical event id. When supplied, the dispatch path reuses it as the ``(webhook_id, event_id)`` idempotency key so a re-dispatch of the same logical event is a true no-op (no duplicate POST, no duplicate delivery row). Used by the VAL-PERF-005 enqueue-latency benchmark to assert a duplicate event_id inserts exactly one row. When omitted, a fresh uuid is generated per call (the production default).

_InjectTestEventRequest.title: _InjectTestEventRequest
_InjectTestEventRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /v1/scheduled/webhooks/inject-test-event``.

The seam dispatches a partner-webhook event at a caller-specified severity
through the REAL :meth:`PartnerWebhookService.dispatch_event` path (it is
NOT a delivery bypass): the service's verified-before-live gating,
subscription match, ``filters.severity_minimum`` /
``filters.environments`` filters, signing-secret cache, signed ML-DSA-44
envelope, ``webhook_deliveries`` row recording, and fire-and-forget
retry schedule all run exactly as for a production emission. The seam
exists ONLY because the M2 lifecycle emits a single partner-webhook event
(``customer.status_changed``) and it is hardcoded to ``severity='info'``
in ``routes/partner.py``, so there is no black-box path to emit a
high-severity partner-webhook event and exercise the
``severity_minimum`` filter's positive half ("receives events at or above
that severity") deterministically. Later milestones (``rl-usage-alerts``
in ``realtime-and-limits``) route REAL high-severity events
(``customer.usage_threshold`` at 100%) to
``partner_webhook_service``; the seam remains for deterministic
validation.
